name: SDN Node Status Flow
description: M1 node-status flow (mount GET /api/v1/node/status): a $HTQ HttpRequest enters on the http-request trigger; foundation/http-route route_node_status decides it as an $APR (GET/HEAD -> route status, anything else STATUS 405); hostcap/node-status reads the node through the policy-mediated READ-ONLY node_status_read.status hostcall (typed $PIV, capability node_status_read; node.peerId and clock.now stamp NODE_ID / GENERATED_AT_MS) and answers an $NHS beside the $APR (or the $APR with STATUS 503 when the host fails); foundation/http-respond respond renders the $HTR (200 / 405 / 503): the $NHS verbatim as FlatBuffers by default, or as JSON when the request asks for it. No ETag: the snapshot changes on every call. Typed contracts 1.0: every edge carries one SDS FlatBuffers type; no JSON travels between nodes (JSON exists only as the client representation http-respond renders on request).

triggers.description: One $HTQ HttpRequest envelope per invocation, pumped by the host at the flow ingress.

api.tagDescription: This node's own live status (wasm; all routing and response shaping run inside the module). Operator-gated (see route anonymous flag) until the $HTQ envelope carries caller-trust information for an anonymous reduced subset.

routes.description: Returns this node's current health snapshot as one $NHS (SDS Node Health Status): uptime, service state, storage totals, disk, network throughput and its recent history. Representation: FlatBuffers by default (?format=flatbuffer or Accept: application/x-flatbuffers); ?format=json or Accept: application/json renders the same record as JSON with the standard's IDL field names (enums by name, byte vectors hex) - rendered by foundation/http-respond, the only place JSON exists. No ETag / If-None-Match: the snapshot changes on every call. Operator-gated (anonymous:false) at the host's auth wall.

200.description: The node's $NHS. Representation: FlatBuffers by default (?format=flatbuffer or Accept: application/x-flatbuffers); ?format=json or Accept: application/json renders the same record as JSON with the standard's IDL field names (enums by name, byte vectors hex) - rendered by foundation/http-respond, the only place JSON exists.

schema.description: The $NHS as JSON (NODE_ID, GENERATED_AT_MS, UPTIME_S, SERVICE_STATE, STORE_TOTAL_*, DISK_*, TOTAL_IN/OUT_BYTES, RATE_IN/OUT_BPS, THROUGHPUT_HISTORY, ...).
$APR (SDS APR.fbs): the refusal record (STATUS / ERROR_CODE / ERROR_MESSAGE)
